scope: The four agent-visible 2.0.0 changes, run for real (actual ffmpeg encodes) by five independent Sonnet agents that read SKILL.md, in fresh fixture folders under /tmp/claude-0/ev24. Graded by the maintainer against each run's verbatim command log (run.md) plus md5 checks of the files that existed before the run -- not by the agents' own summaries.

detail.prompt: Trim clip.mp4 to the first 5 seconds and save it as short.mp4. (short.mp4 already existed)
detail.evidence: cut.py was refused (kind input, 'refusing to overwrite existing output'); the agent re-ran with --overwrite because the user named the path, and its final message says the old short.mp4 was replaced. md5 of short.mp4 changed, as intended.

detail.prompt: Make a vertical 9:16 version of talk.mp4 for Reels. (talk_vertical.mp4 already existed)
detail.evidence: render.py --template reels wrote talk_reels.mp4; talk_vertical.mp4 md5 unchanged; the final message names the untouched file.

detail.prompt: Crop clip.mp4 to a square and keep the quality high — use CRF 16.
detail.evidence: fit.py --aspect 1:1 --fit crop --quality 16; no --crf anywhere in the log.

detail.prompt: Is wide.mp4 HDR? (BT.2020 primaries, BT.709 transfer)
detail.evidence: Read probe's hdr: false and hdr_format 'BT.2020 SDR' and answered 'not HDR'.
detail.note: It called the file 'safe to send as-is' to an SDR-only client; BT.2020 primaries can still shift colour in a BT.709-only pipeline. Added to references/gotchas.md #hdr-and-colour (color.py --to-sdr before a BT.709 delivery; export.py only retags). Also found: export.py's warning still calls such a source "HDR (BT.2020 SDR)", 1.x wording -- queued for 2.1.0. Not a 2.0 regression. Checked the fix itself: color.py --to-sdr on the BT.2020 SDR fixture writes bt709/bt709 H.264, but its filter chain also runs the HDR tone map (tonemap=hable, npl=1000) on a source that is already SDR; a BT.2020 SDR input should only need the gamut conversion. Queued for 2.1.0 with the export.py wording, pending a measured before/after.

detail.prompt: iphone.mp4 looks washed out on my laptop. Make a normal version I can post anywhere. (HDR10/PQ)
detail.evidence: probe found HDR10/PQ; color.py --to-sdr; output bt709/bt709 H.264; check + look run.

not_measured: One run per prompt (no repeats), one model (Sonnet), no MCP path; the trigger/routing set was not re-run at 2.0.0.
follow_ups: export.py warning wording for BT.2020 SDR sources (says 'HDR')
color.py --to-sdr applies the PQ/HLG tone map to BT.2020 SDR input; gamut-convert only, with a measured before/after
